Q: How can you export the Visual Studio Code extension list? A:

https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editor/extension-gallery#_workspace-recommended-extensions

A better way to share extension list is to create workspace-based extension set for your colleagues:

  1. Generate a list of extensions via code --list-extensions | xargs -L 1 echo code --install-extension
    If you get error verify that your $PATH contains Visual Studio Code entry C:\Program Files\Microsoft VS Code\bin\, if no go into command palette (Ctrl + Shift + P)

    and run Shell Command: Install 'code' command in PATH

  2. Run Extensions: Configure Recommended Extensions (Workspace Folder) from command palette and put extensions into the generated .vscode/extensions.json file and push it into you VCS

    {
    "recommendations": [
        "eg2.tslint",
        "dbaeumer.vscode-eslint",
        "msjsdiag.debugger-for-chrome"
    ]
}

Now your colleagues will have prompt in VSCode to install recommended extensions upon opening repository.

Q: Do media types provide for personal use parameters on a standard type? A:

Can you edit your question to clarify the following: 1. Where exactly in RFC 2045 are the media types you talk about defined? 2. Where does it mention the 'personal use tree'? I not denying a thing like that exists, but the RFC is about email messages and their structure. So: 3. What is the relation between this message structure and the web browser recognizing the mime type?

Anyway, a PNG image is a mime type in itself. No need to further qualify it. In other words: An image can only have one mime type. Compare it to a file extension: A file can only have one extension.
